es.term: Depósito de complejos inmunes (hipersensibilidad tipo III)
es.summary: Formación de complejos antígeno‑anticuerpo que se depositan en vasos y tejidos, activando complemento y provocando inflamación.
key_points: Activación del complemento genera quimiotaxis de neutrófilos
Daño vascular produce edema, dolor y posible necrosis
Se asocia a enfermedades como lupus eritematoso sistémico, vasculitis y serum sickness
El diagnóstico combina clínica y pruebas de laboratorio (C3, C4, anticuerpos)

pathophysiology: Antígeno + anticuerpo forman complejos inmunes de tamaño intermedio
Los complejos circulan y se depositan en paredes capilares o glomerulares
Activan la vía clásica del complemento (C1‑C4)
C5a atrae neutrófilos que liberan enzimas y radicales libres
Daño endotelial produce edema, hemorragia y necrosis tisular
risk_factors: Deficiencia de factores reguladores del complemento
signs_symptoms: Dolor abdominal o hematuria si afecta riñón
diagnostics: Biopsia de piel/riñón: depósito granular de IgG y C3 en inmunofluorescencia
Niveles bajos de C3 y C4 en sangre
Pruebas de anticuerpos específicos (ANA, anti‑DNA, anti‑GBM)
Exámenes de función renal: creatinina y proteinuria
treatment: Antihistamínicos y AINES para manejo sintomático
nursing_care: Evaluar dolor, edema y cambios cutáneos cada 4 h
Monitorear signos vitales, especialmente presión arterial y temperatura
Controlar ingreso de líquidos y balance hídrico
Observar resultados de laboratorio (C3, C4, creatinina) y notificar alteraciones
Mantener posición cómoda que reduzca presión sobre áreas inflamadas
patient_teaching: Explicar la naturaleza de la enfermedad y la importancia de la adherencia al tratamiento
Enseñar a reconocer signos de empeoramiento: aumento de edema, hematuria, fiebre alta
Instruir sobre la toma correcta de medicamentos y efectos secundarios comunes
Promover hidratación adecuada y dieta baja en sodio para proteger la función renal
Fomentar evitar exposición a agentes desencadenantes (fármacos nuevos, infecciones)

related_to: Inflamación tisular por depósito de complejos inmunes
evidenced_by: Rubor e hinchazón en zona afectada
outcomes: Control del dolor: nivel de dolor ≤3/10 en escala numérica en 48 h
Reducción de inflamación: disminución del edema visible en 72 h

interventions.action: Evaluar intensidad y localización del dolor cada 4 h usando escala numérica
interventions.rationale: Permite monitorear la respuesta al tratamiento y ajustar intervenciones

interventions.action: Administrar analgésicos según prescripción y registrar efecto
interventions.rationale: Alivio del dolor facilita la movilidad y reduce el estrés fisiológico

interventions.action: Aplicar compresas frías o tibias según indicación para disminuir inflamación
interventions.rationale: El frío vasoconstrictor reduce edema; el calor mejora la circulación cuando sea apropiado

interventions.action: Enseñar técnicas de relajación y respiración profunda
interventions.rationale: Disminuye la percepción del dolor mediante modulación del sistema nervioso

interventions.action: Promover posición de reposo con elevación del miembro afectado
interventions.rationale: Reduce la presión capilar y ayuda a controlar el edema

related_to: Depósito de complejos inmunes con daño cutáneo
outcomes: Sin signos de infección (fiebre, pus, aumento de dolor) durante la hospitalización
Cultivos negativos si se realizan pruebas de control

interventions.action: Realizar higiene de la piel y de sitios de inserción de catéteres con técnica aséptica
interventions.rationale: Previene colonización bacteriana en áreas vulnerables

interventions.action: Monitorear temperatura corporal cada 4 h y reportar fiebre >38 °C
interventions.rationale: Detección temprana de infección permite intervención oportuna

interventions.action: Evaluar integridad de la piel y registrar cualquier ruptura o exudado
interventions.rationale: Las úlceras son puertas de entrada para microorganismos

interventions.action: Educar al paciente sobre signos de infección y la importancia de reportarlos inmediatamente
interventions.rationale: Facilita la detección precoz y el tratamiento rápido

interventions.action: Mantener una nutrición adecuada y control de glucosa en pacientes con corticoides
interventions.rationale: Mejora la respuesta inmune y reduce el riesgo de infecciones

en.summary: Formation of antigen‑antibody complexes that deposit in vessels and tissues, activating complement and causing inflammation.
key_points: Vascular damage causes edema, pain and possible necrosis
Associated with diseases such as systemic lupus erythematosus, vasculitis and serum sickness
Diagnosis combines clinical presentation and laboratory tests (C3, C4, antibodies)

pathophysiology: Antigen + antibody form intermediate‑sized immune complexes
The complexes circulate and deposit in capillary or glomerular walls
They activate the classical complement pathway (C1‑C4)
C5a attracts neutrophils that release enzymes and free radicals
Endothelial damage produces edema, hemorrhage and tissue necrosis
signs_symptoms: Abdominal pain or hematuria if kidneys are involved
diagnostics: Skin/renal biopsy: granular IgG and C3 deposits on immunofluorescence
Low serum C3 and C4 levels
Renal function tests: creatinine and proteinuria
treatment: Antihistamines and NSAIDs for symptomatic relief
nursing_care: Assess pain, edema and skin changes every 4 h
Monitor vital signs, especially blood pressure and temperature
Control fluid intake and fluid balance
Observe laboratory results (C3, C4, creatinine) and report abnormalities
Maintain a comfortable position that reduces pressure on inflamed areas
patient_teaching: Explain the nature of the disease and the importance of treatment adherence
Teach recognition of worsening signs: increased edema, hematuria, high fever
Instruct on proper medication use and common side effects
Promote adequate hydration and a low‑sodium diet to protect renal function
Encourage avoidance of triggering agents (new drugs, infections)

related_to: Tissue inflammation from immune complex deposition
evidenced_by: Redness and swelling in affected area
outcomes: Pain control: pain level ≤3/10 on numeric scale within 48 h
Reduction of inflammation: visible edema decrease within 72 h

interventions.action: Assess pain intensity and location every 4 h using numeric scale
interventions.rationale: Allows monitoring of treatment response and adjustment of interventions

interventions.action: Administer analgesics as prescribed and record effect
interventions.rationale: Pain relief facilitates mobility and reduces physiological stress

interventions.action: Apply cold or warm compresses as indicated to reduce inflammation
interventions.rationale: Cold vasoconstricts to reduce edema; heat improves circulation when appropriate

interventions.action: Teach relaxation and deep breathing techniques
interventions.rationale: Reduces pain perception through nervous system modulation

interventions.action: Promote rest position with elevation of affected limb
interventions.rationale: Reduces capillary pressure and helps control edema

related_to: Immune complex deposition with skin damage
outcomes: No signs of infection (fever, pus, increased pain) during hospitalization
Negative cultures if control tests are performed

interventions.action: Perform skin hygiene and catheter insertion site care with aseptic technique
interventions.rationale: Prevents bacterial colonization in vulnerable areas

interventions.action: Monitor body temperature every 4 h and report fever >38 °C
interventions.rationale: Early detection of infection allows timely intervention

interventions.action: Assess skin integrity and record any breaks or exudate
interventions.rationale: Ulcers are entry points for microorganisms

interventions.action: Educate patient on infection signs and importance of immediate reporting
interventions.rationale: Facilitates early detection and rapid treatment

interventions.action: Maintain adequate nutrition and glucose control in patients on corticosteroids
interventions.rationale: Improves immune response and reduces infection risk

sources.name: Pharmacology for Nurses: Introduction to the Inflammatory Response and Anti-inflammatory Drugs

sections.risk_factors.1.quote: It is used to manage conditions such as systemic lupus erythematosus (SLE) and rheumatoid arthritis (RA).

sections.signs_symptoms.0.quote: The nurse will also check the skin and mucous membranes for any lesions, purpura, urticaria, dermatitis, inflammation , or discharge.

sections.signs_symptoms.2.quote: Take the patient’s temperature and assess their joints for tenderness, edema, warmth, or limited range of motion.

sections.treatment.0.quote: Glucocorticoids , also known as corticosteroids or simply steroids, are a class of anti-inflammatory drugs that mimic the action of naturally occurring hormones produced by the adrenal glands.

sections.patient_teaching.1.quote: The patient should be educated on signs and symptoms of infection and the need to immediately report symptoms, such as a fever of 100.5°F (38°C) or greater, decreased urine output, bloody urine, flu-like symptoms, tenderness around the transplanted orga

sections.patient_teaching.2.quote: The nurse or prescriber must educate the patient to take their medications as prescribed, despite any side effects, as skipping a dose can result in a flare-up or worsening of the condition the drug is intended to treat.
